OBJECTIVES

The applications for graphing trigonometric functions like these are numerous.
INTRODUCTIONM
The alternating current in an electrical circuit is described using trigonometric equations and graphs.
Equations of this form can also be used as mathematical models for sound waves.
Let's Begin the Lesson on GRAPHING TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS.Y................
LESSON MENU
Trigonometric functions can be graphed using a table of values for the point coordinates.
DISCUSSION

POINT COORDINATES - Functions may be graphed by choosing an X value and solving to get a Y value. These values become the X-coordinates and corresponding Y-coordinates needed to plot points on the rectangular coordinate system.
The sine and cosine functions may also be graphed by using the unit circle.
Let's start by graphing the sine function as Y = sin X.
Start with an angle measurement of zero on the unit circle. The measurement of the angle is the X value and the sine of the measurement is the Y value.
As the angle increases to p/4 the sine values increase to S2/2 or aproximately 0.7..
The sine value becomes 1 at a p /2 angle.
The angle continues to increase to 3 p /4 but the sine values decreases.......
When the angle reaches p the sine value is zero..
As the angle increases to 5 p/4 the sine values become negative.
When the angle reaches 7p/4 the sine value returns to -S2/2.
The sine value returns to zero at 2p. One complete revolution on the unit circle yields one complete sine wave...
The graph of Y = sin X may be extended. The values continue to repeat and never go above 1 or below -1.
Since all possible values for Y = sin X can be found between 0 and 2 , we say that Y = sin X has a period of 2 ..

The period of a function indicates the point when it begins to repeat. It is the final minus the initial X value for the graph. For example, the values for Y = sin X begin to repeat after 2 so the period is 2 .
The amplitude (A) of a function is half the distance between the Y values of the highest (H) and lowest (L) (peak points).
The amplitude for Y = sin X is 1 since the highest point is 1 and the lowest point is -1.
The graph of Y = cos X is similar in shape to Y = sin X.
In fact, the cosine graph looks like the sine graph but with a horizontal shift. Y = cos XX
The unit circle may be used to graph Y = cos X as it was used to graph Y = sin X.
Although the shape of the cosine curve is different, the period is also 2 since the curve begins to repeat after this point..
The amplitude is 1 since Y = cos X stays between 1 and -1.

DEFINITION

ASYMPTOTE - Asymptotes are lines which identify the boundaries of the graph of a function. The graph approaches the asymptote but never touches or crosses this line because the function is undefined at that value.

AMPLITUDE, PERIOD & PHASE SHIFT
The amplitude of the sine and cosine functions changes depending on the coefficient written next to the function.
DISCUSSION
This number determines the amplitude of the function. A 1 indicates an amplitude of 1 and a 3 indicates an amplitude of 3.
Notice that the period stays the same, only the height of the curve changes.
Here are some more examples................................
If the coefficient written next to the function is negative, the graph is reflected in the X-axis. The amplitude always remains positive.
The period of the function changes depending on the coefficient next to the variable.
The new period is found by dividing 2p by this number.
This method is used for sine, cosine, cosecant, and secant functions.

Along with changes in amplitude and period, trigonometric graphs may also shift horizontally along the X-axis.
A horizontal shift is called the phase shift.
A phase shift occurs when a number is added to the variable.
The value of the phase shift is added to each X or angle measurement on the basic graph. For example, Y = sin X is zero at , and Y = sin (X + /2) is zero at - /2 or /2.
Equations like these can be rewritten in order to find the phase shift.
The other points on the graph are found by adding the value of the phase shift to each X or angle measurement on the basic graph of Y = cos X.
